title: 2026 U.S. Senate election in Tennessee
description: Tennessee will elect one U.S. senator in 2026 for the state’s Class II seat, currently held by Republican Bill Hagerty. The race is widely viewed as safely Republican: Cook Political Report rates it Solid R, and Tennessee’s recent federal elections have strongly favored Republicans. The main contrast is between Hagerty’s incumbency and a Democratic field that is trying to make the race competitive in a state that has not elected a Democrat to the U.S. Senate since 1990.
polling_note: No public polling found for this race as of 2026-05-18.

candidates.name: Bill Hagerty

reviews.summary: This is a well-researched and comprehensive profile of the 2026 Tennessee U.S. Senate race. The incumbent (Bill Hagerty) and five Democratic challengers are documented with strong, current sourcing from official campaign sites, government records, and credible news outlets. The profile demonstrates good-faith research effort across 12+ policy domains per candidate, with appropriately marked low-confidence positions where public statements are genuinely unavailable. Language is notably neutral and nonpartisan throughout—no loaded terminology, no asymmetric framing between candidates, and no value-laden adjectives applied selectively. Background information is well-documented and consistent with cited sources. Minor gaps on some candidates' climate/energy and tech positions are appropriately flagged as 'no public position found' rather than asserted as absences, reflecting the agent's transparent search methodology.

forecast.rationale: No public polling is available for this race, which increases uncertainty and lowers confidence. Even so, the available race description and state context strongly favor Republicans: Tennessee has voted reliably Republican in recent federal elections, the seat is held by incumbent Republican Bill Hagerty, and the race is widely described as safely Republican, including a Solid R characterization in the provided race data. The Democratic field appears multi-candidate and lacks evidence here of a top-tier statewide challenger, while Hagerty benefits from incumbency in a state where Democrats have not won a U.S. Senate race since 1990. Taken together, the non-polling fundamentals point to a very strong Republican advantage.
